questions.html: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW)?
questions.hint: Tim Berners Lee invented the World Wide Web (WWW).

questions.html: Which cable is used to connect television sets to home antennas?
questions.hint: Coaxial cable is used to connect television sets to home antennas. Has a copper wire inside with insulation on top.

questions.html: Coaxial cable has a data transfer speed of:
questions.hint: Coaxial cable has a data transfer speed of 10 Mbps. It is classified into Thinnet and Thicknet.

questions.html: Twisted pair cable has how many wires twisted together?
questions.hint: Twisted pair cable has 8 wires twisted together to ignore electromagnetic interference.

questions.html: Which type of twisted pair cable is covered by an additional jacket to protect from external interference?
questions.hint: STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) is covered by an additional jacket for protection. UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) is modern, lower cost, easy to install.

questions.html: Fiber optic cable transmits data using:
questions.hint: Fiber optic cable is made of strands of glass and uses pulses of LIGHT to transmit data.

questions.html: Fiber optic cable is mainly used in:
questions.hint: Fiber optic cable is mainly used in WAN (Wide Area Network) and is placed deep underground.

questions.html: Which type of fiber optic cable is used for long distance, high cost transmission?
questions.hint: Single-mode fiber = long distance, high cost. Multimode fiber = short distance, low cost.

questions.html: USB stands for:
questions.hint: USB = Universal Serial Bus. Used to connect keyboard, mouse, and peripheral devices.

questions.html: The latest version of USB with a data transfer rate of 4.85 Gbps is:
questions.hint: USB 3.0 is the latest version mentioned, with a data transfer rate of 4.85 Gbps.

questions.html: Which cable sends 1 bit at a time?
questions.hint: Serial cable sends 1 bit at a time. Parallel cable sends 8 bits at a time. Example: RS232 cable is a serial cable.

questions.html: Ethernet cable is a type of:
questions.hint: Ethernet cable is a type of twisted pair cable, most common for home/office LAN.

questions.html: RJ45 connector is also called:
questions.hint: RJ45 connector is also called an 8P8C connector — a small plastic cube with 8 pins.

questions.html: RJ in RJ45 stands for:
questions.hint: RJ = Registered Jack. 45 = interface standard.

questions.html: Which tool is used to connect the patch wire and RJ45 connector?
questions.hint: A crimping tool is used to connect the patch wire and RJ45 connector, locking the connector onto the cable.

questions.html: Which registered jack is most popular for home and office landline phones?
questions.hint: RJ-11 is the most popular modern registered jack, used for landline phones. Has 6 pins.

questions.html: RJ-21 is also known as:
questions.hint: RJ-21 is also called Champ Connector or Amphenol Connector. Has 50 pins (25 at each end).

questions.html: Which wiring technique is used for connecting a PC/NIC card to a hub?
questions.hint: Straight-through wiring: same sequence at both ends, used for PC/NIC card to a hub. Most common.

questions.html: Cross-over wiring is also called:
questions.hint: Cross-over wiring is also called Null modem cable. Used to connect two computers directly without a hub.

questions.html: Roll-over wiring is used to connect:
options: b) A PC to a hub
c) A device console port for programming changes
d) A modem to a router
questions.hint: Roll-over wiring (also called Console cable) is used to connect a device console port for programming changes. Pin 1 connects to Pin 8, opposite sequence.

questions.ans: Coaxial cable is used to connect television sets to home antennas. It has a copper wire inside with insulation on top. Data transfer speed is 10 Mbps. Coaxial cables are classified into Thinnet and Thicknet. They are difficult to install and maintain compared to modern cables.

questions.q: What is a twisted pair cable?
questions.ans: Twisted pair cable has 8 wires twisted together to reduce electromagnetic interference. There are two types: UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) — modern, lower cost, easy installation; and STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) — covered by an additional jacket to protect from external interference. Ethernet cable is a type of twisted pair cable.

questions.q: What is a fiber optic cable?
questions.ans: Fiber optic cable is made of strands of glass and uses pulses of LIGHT (instead of electrical signals) to transmit data. It is mainly used in WAN (Wide Area Network) and is placed deep underground. There are two types: Single-mode (long distance, high cost) and Multimode (short distance, low cost). Fiber optic cable is easy to maintain.

RJ45 connector is a small plastic cube with 8 pins, connected to each end of the Ethernet cable. It is also called an 8P8C connector. It is plugged into the Ethernet port of a network card. RJ stands for Registered Jack, and 45 refers to the interface standard.

questions.q: Differentiate straight-through wiring and cross-over wiring.
questions.ans:
Straight-through Wiring: Wires are in the SAME sequence at both ends. Pin 1 at one end connects to Pin 1 at the other end. Used for connecting a PC/NIC card to a hub. Most common wiring type.

Cross-over Wiring: Used to connect TWO computers directly without a hub. TX and RX lines are crossed. One end uses T568A, the other T568B. Also called Null modem cable.

questions.q: Explain the different types of network cables.
questions.ans:
There are 6 main types of network cables:
1. Coaxial Cable — Connects TV sets to antennas, copper wire with insulation, 10 Mbps, classified into Thinnet and Thicknet.
2. Twisted Pair Cable — 8 wires twisted together, types: UTP and STP.
3. Fiber Optic Cable — Uses pulses of light, made of glass, used in WAN, types: Single-mode and Multimode.
4. USB Cables — Connects keyboard, mouse, peripherals; USB 3.0 gives 4.85 Gbps.
5. Serial and Parallel Cables — Serial sends 1 bit at a time, Parallel sends 8 bits at a time; used before Ethernet.
6. Ethernet Cable — A type of twisted pair cable, most common for LAN, standards: Cat 3, Cat 5, Cat 6, Cat 6e, Cat 7.

questions.q: Write a note on the Ethernet cabling components.
questions.ans:
Ethernet cabling has 4 main components:
1. Patch Cable (Twisted Pair) — Made of 8 wires in different colours (4 solid, 4 striped). Standards: Cat 3 to Cat 7.
2. RJ45 Connector — Small plastic cube with 8 pins, also called 8P8C connector, connected to each end of the cable.
3. Ethernet Port — Opening on network card that accepts the RJ45 connector; found on PCs, routers, switches. Green LED = connected, orange blinking LED = Internet connected.
4. Crimping Tool — Physical tool used to lock the RJ45 connector onto the patch wire.

questions.q: Explain the three Ethernet cable wiring techniques.
questions.ans:
There are 3 wiring techniques used for Ethernet cabling:
1. Straight-Through Wiring — Same wire sequence at both ends (Pin 1 to Pin 1). Used to connect a PC/NIC card to a hub. Most common technique.
2. Cross-Over Wiring — Used to connect two computers directly without a hub. TX and RX lines are crossed (Pin 1 & 2 of one end to Pin 3 & 6 of the other). One end uses T568A, the other T568B. Also called Null modem cable.
3. Roll-Over Wiring — Wires in OPPOSITE sequence at either end (Pin 1 to Pin 8, Pin 2 to Pin 7, etc.). Used to connect a device console port for programming changes. Also called Console cable, usually flat and light blue.

questions.q: Explain in detail the types of network cables used to connect computers in a network.
questions.ans:
A computer network needs a physical connection — wired or wireless. Wired networks are faster and more secure but more expensive for large areas; wireless enables more devices to share resources remotely. There are 6 main types of wired network cables:

1. Coaxial Cable — Connects TV sets to home antennas. Has a copper wire inside with insulation. Data transfer speed: 10 Mbps. Classified into Thinnet and Thicknet. Difficult to install and maintain.

2. Twisted Pair Cable — Has 8 wires twisted together to reduce electromagnetic interference. Two types: UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) — modern, low cost, easy installation; and STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) — has additional protective jacket.

3. Fiber Optic Cable — Made of strands of glass, uses pulses of LIGHT to transmit data. Mainly used in WAN, placed deep underground. Types: Single-mode (long distance, high cost) and Multimode (short distance, low cost). Easy to maintain.

4. USB Cables — Universal Serial Bus, connects keyboard, mouse, peripheral devices. Micro USB for mobiles, GPS, cameras. USB 3.0 gives 4.85 Gbps transfer rate.

5. Serial and Parallel Cables — Used before Ethernet. Serial sends 1 bit at a time (e.g., RS232); Parallel sends 8 bits at a time, used for printers and disk drives.

6. Ethernet Cable — A type of twisted pair cable, the most common cable for home/office LAN. Standards: Cat 3, Cat 5, Cat 6, Cat 6e, Cat 7 — higher category means faster speed and higher frequency.

questions.q: Describe RJ45 connectors, wiring schemes, and the three Ethernet wiring techniques in detail.
questions.ans:
Ethernet cabling has 4 main components: Patch Cable (twisted pair, 8 coloured wires, Cat 3–Cat 7 standards), RJ45 Connector (small plastic cube with 8 pins, also called 8P8C connector, plugged into the Ethernet port of a network card), Ethernet Port (opening on network cards, routers, switches; green LED = connected, blinking orange = Internet active), and Crimping Tool (locks the RJ45 connector onto the patch wire).

Wiring Schemes: T568A and T568B are two colour-code schemes for wiring the RJ45 connector. Ethernet uses only 2 of the 4 wire pairs (orange and green). TX = transmit, RX = receive. Pin 1 = TX+, Pin 2 = TX-, Pin 3 = RX+, Pin 6 = RX-; pins 4, 5, 7, 8 are reserved.

Three Wiring Techniques:
1. Straight-Through Wiring — Same sequence at both ends (Pin 1 to Pin 1). Used to connect a PC/NIC card to a hub. Most common.
2. Cross-Over Wiring — Connects two computers directly without a hub; TX/RX lines crossed; one end T568A, other T568B. Also called Null modem cable.
3. Roll-Over Wiring — Opposite sequence at either end (Pin 1 to Pin 8). Used to connect a device console port for programming changes. Also called Console cable, usually flat and light blue.
